name: Tertullus (lawyer)
title: The Jews' spokesman against Paul
summary: Tertullus was a professional Roman lawyer (orator) hired by the high priest Ananias and the Jewish elders to present charges against the apostle Paul before the Roman governor Felix in Caesarea. He was known for his rhetorical style and flattery, but his accusations against Paul were not proven.

keyEvents.title: The charges against Paul
keyEvents.description: Tertullus presented the charges against Paul to Governor Felix, accusing him of being a plague, an agitator among the Jews, and a leader of the Nazarene sect.

keyEvents.title: Flattery of Felix
keyEvents.description: Tertullus began his speech with excessive flattery toward Felix, praising him for the peace and reforms he had supposedly brought to the nation.

keyEvents.title: Accusation of temple desecration
keyEvents.description: Tertullus claimed that Paul had attempted to desecrate the temple, which was a serious charge that could carry the death penalty.

keyEvents.title: Paul's defense
keyEvents.description: After Tertullus' speech, Paul was given the opportunity to defend himself and refuted all the charges point by point.
